inorder.why: In-order visits the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. This tree is a binary search tree, so that order is sorted.

preorder.why: Pre-order visits the node first, then its left subtree, then its right subtree.

why-sorted.why: The BST property orders each node against its whole subtrees, and visiting left, node, right respects that at every level.

degenerate.why: Each new key is larger than everything before it, so the tree degenerates into a chain going right. Searching it is a linked-list walk. Balanced trees (like the red-black tree behind TreeMap) prevent this.

treemap-get.why: TreeMap is a red-black tree, which keeps itself balanced, so its height stays O(log n).

level-order.why: Nodes are processed in the order they were discovered, level by level: first in, first out.

height.why: A tree is as tall as its taller subtree plus the node itself.
